Simplification review of this packet's change surface only (commits 20b0376a, 0dcb9d1f, 639fb9f4, d2362063, 5b0c53c7, 833742cd), against three named duplication candidates. VERDICT: LEAVE ALL THREE. (1) THE THREE AMORTIZED SWEEPS -- DedupeIndex.Record, InMemoryAck.Acknowledge, NudgeRegistry.gcLocked -- share a SHAPE, not logic, and premature abstraction applies rather than the copy-paste ban. Read side by side, every parameter that could carry a bug already differs: value type (map[string]time.Time twice vs map[NudgeRef]nudgeEntry, where the timestamp is a struct field), key type, eviction predicate in BOTH multiplier and boundary strictness (t.Before(now-2*window) / t.Before(now-30d) / now.Sub(issuedAt) >= ttl -- note strict vs non-strict), cadence source (instance field d.window and r.ttl vs package consts ackSweepInterval), and call position (tail-of-write vs a separate gcLocked called at the HEAD of Mint). What is literally identical is the compound guard plus two bookkeeping lines. Read-only residual-flake review of tests/stress at HEAD d287b4f1, answering three questions posed after the two G084 stress fixes landed. ZERO code changed: no production file, no test file, no scopes.md; the only file this run wrote is this state.json. The stress lane was NOT run (explicitly out of scope), so every claim below is derived from source and from the lane's own runner script, and nothing here is presented as an executed measurement. (1) THIRD RESIDUAL RISK -- YES, and it is the SAME defect class the fix just closed, left in a third file. The GOMAXPROCS worker cap was applied to exactly 2 of the 5 stress files that spawn a worker pool and then assert a wall-clock latency percentile: assistant_facade_p95_test.go:200-203 and openknowledge_p95_test.go:147-150 are capped; tests/stress/assistant/http_turn_stress_test.go:52 (httpStressDefaultWorkers=16) and :118 (workers := httpStressDefaultWorkers, no cap, package imports no runtime) is NOT, and asserts a single-round wall-clock p95 against a 50ms budget at :207. It is in the lane: scripts/runtime/go-stress.sh:62 enumerates go list ./tests/stress/... so every subpackage runs. It is the highest-risk uncapped one because its measured region is CPU-bound -- a constant-time facade behind one global mutex (stressFacade.Handle:67-71) -- which is exactly the profile that turned a wall-clock sample into a run-queue measurement in the two fixed files. The other two uncapped 32-worker files are NOT comparable and are explicitly rated LOW: assistant_retrieval_p95_test.go:58 and assistant_weather_p95_test.go:55 both spend their measured region asleep in time.After (1-41ms injected jitter) against 5s / 3s budgets, and sleeping goroutines do not contend for cores. Ranked second, and a DIFFERENT class: ml_readiness_timeout_stress_test.go:182-190 is a single-sample TWO-SIDED wall-clock bound, elapsed must land in [boundary-500ms, boundary+2s] with boundary=2s (smackerel.sh:2627 sets SMACKEREL_ML_READINESS_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE=2s), so there is no percentile smoothing at all and one ~2s stall fails it; recorded prior observation was 2.000778326s. Ranked third: proactive/proactive_hotpath_test.go:59-61 asserts p99 (tighter percentile than p95) at 5ms over 50k single-threaded iterations on the very hot path the O(n^2) sweep defect lived on, and the maps grow to ~55k live entries because the rate-limited sweep now correctly declines to scan inside the 6h window. Also noted: drive/drive_scale_stress_test.go:115-140, a 20ms-deadline cleanup asserted by EXACT failure count under a 500ms outer guard, plus an ordering assumption that the connection delete precedes the artifact delete. RULED OUT by search rather than assumed: zero t.Parallel, zero fixed ports (only 127.0.0.1:0 and t.TempDir), and go-stress.sh:84-91 runs packages sequentially, so cross-package port/tmpdir/CPU interference is not a live vector. (2) CAN THE SWEEP-COUNTER REGRESSIONS FLAKE -- NO, and the reason is stronger than 'they assert a counter'. Both freeze the clock and the rate-limit gate reads that same injected clock, not time.Now: dedupe.go:68+81 uses d.clock() for both now and the !now.Before(d.nextSweep) gate, suppression.go:57+62 likewise, nudgeref.go:174+182 likewise. With a frozen clock the trajectory is forced -- one sweep fires when the map first exceeds 4096, nextSweep moves to now+window, and every later call sees now.Before(nextSweep) true -- so sweeps is exactly 1, deterministically, and the assertion sweeps>1 can only trip on a real regression of the gate. The len(entries)==burst precondition is also safe: Mint could in principle collide, but nudgeref.go:107-114 retries on collision, so 20000 Mints yield 20000 entries. TWO HONEST LIMITS, neither of which is a flake. First, the assertions are one-sided (sweeps>1 only); a regression that disables sweeping outright would pass them. That direction is covered elsewhere -- dedupe_gc_test.go:46 for the index, nudgeref_test.go:93 for the registry, suppression_test.go:10 for the ack -- so the pair is complete only when read together with those three. Second, suppression_test.go:10 now silently depends on 2*ackRetention > ackSweepInterval (30d*2 vs 24h, a 60x margin); shortening ackRetention below 12h would break it via the new rate limit rather than via eviction, which would read as a confusing failure. (3) WHEN THE BEST-OF-3 P95 ESTIMATOR MASKS A REAL SLOWDOWN. The published rationale -- contention can only inflate a wall-clock sample, so the minimum is the least-biased estimate -- holds ONLY when the regression is present in every round. Five conditions break that. (a) INTERMITTENT REGRESSION: if a slowdown manifests per-round with probability p (lock convoy needing an interleaving, a size-triggered rehash, a background-GC-timed eviction), best-of-3 misses it with probability (1-p)^3 -- 12.5% at p=0.5, 34% at p=0.3. The estimator is unbiased against host noise and biased AGAINST detecting stochastic regressions. (b) SUB-THRESHOLD MAGNITUDE: the comment records p50 ~70us against a 5ms budget, so a regression must be roughly 70x before it can trip the gate at all; this dominates and is independent of the estimator. (c) TAIL-ONLY REGRESSION: p99 and max are computed and logged but never asserted (openknowledge_p95_test.go:160-171, assistant_facade_p95_test.go:222-233), so any regression confined to under 5% of turns is invisible at p95 by construction. (d) WARM-STATE SELECTION: min-of-N systematically picks the warmest round, which is exactly the class of regression that shows up as first-use cost -- a new sync.Once, a lazily compiled regex, initial arena or map growth -- because the shared registry/cfg (openknowledge) and the shared facade/store/router (facade) are constructed ONCE outside the round loop and pay any one-time cost in round 1 only. (e) ROUNDS ARE NOT IDENTICAL in the facade variant despite the comment saying so: memStore conversations and stubRouter.calls carry across rounds, so round 1 ramps its 5-turn window from empty while rounds 2-3 start at steady state. That effect is bounded and I am not inflating it -- the ramp is ~5 of 1500 turns per user and cannot move p95 -- but it does falsify the 'identical rounds' premise the unbiasedness argument rests on. Also structural, not a masking condition but worth stating precisely: the early break at bestP95<=budget means the passing path measures exactly ONE round, so the p50/p95/p99 drift telemetry that goal G3 promises the operator is single-round in every green run; and 'min of per-round p95' is by construction a biased-low estimator of the true p95, so it should never be reported as if it were the measured p95. NO FIX APPLIED, deliberately: the one change worth making (capping http_turn_stress_test.go workers at GOMAXPROCS, ~3 lines) sits behind the stress build tag, so the only test that could prove it is the stress lane, which this run was told not to run. Shipping an unproven edit to a stress-tagged file would be exactly the unverified change the evidence standard forbids, so it is routed instead.

Root cause, proven this session: the guard resolves `sp=(.scopeProgress // .certification.scopeProgress // [])` then takes `sp_len=$(… | jq 'length')` WITHOUT type-checking. For this packet that expression resolves to the OBJECT {"total":1,"done":1,"inProgress":0,"notStarted":0} (jq type=object), so `length` returns the KEY COUNT 4 rather than a scope count; the guard then indexes elements that are numbers, jq raises 'Cannot index number with string "dependsOn"', and the script exits 5, which state-transition-guard.sh Check 44 converts into 'Plan dependency depth violation … every consumer-visible scope sits behind >=3 foundation scopes'. That message is FALSE here: the packet has exactly ONE scope, and Check 46 (vertical-delivery-plan-guard) independently PASSES with 'first usable increment is early (scope 1 of 1); no horizontal chain'. With one scope there cannot be three foundation scopes behind it. The guard's own header documents that a single-file scopes.md plan should be a NO-OP, so the intended behaviour is no-op, not block. Proposed one-line fix in the bubbles source repo: no-op unless the resolved scopeProgress has jq type == "array". NOT patched locally — .github/bubbles/ is an installed framework artifact and must be refreshed through the installer, so a local edit would be silently reverted on the next upgrade.
